periods.analysis: At 91.6%, Harborview’s Federal Graduation Rate opened this run above the 90% target and firmly in green. This is a strong starting point for a fast-growing city system, especially with midyear enrollment churn around the airport and seaport employment corridors. The Class of 2024 credit audit showed the best traction among students served through the Harborview Success Coaches at Northport, Bayside, and East Channel high schools. I am encouraged, but I am not casual about it: a green graduation rate still depends on daily attendance, clean transcripts, and timely interventions for every senior who is one illness, housing move, or failed course away from the line.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the senior credit-review cadence by keeping monthly transcript checks at every comprehensive high school and adding a principal-level exception review for students within one credit of completion. Extend the Success Coach model to the two highest-mobility feeder zones, with attendance liaisons sharing weekly chronic-absence flags before students become graduation risks.

periods.analysis: The rate moved from 91.6% to 91.3%, a quarter-over-quarter change of -0.3 points, and remains green above the 90% target. That small decline is not a cause for alarm, but it is a reminder that graduation is earned student by student, not protected by last quarter’s headline. Counselors reported that late fall withdrawals and credit-transfer delays were concentrated among students moving through the South Harbor and Airport Way housing markets. The system is still performing well, but our watch item is the handoff between attendance recovery, alternative credit, and verified diploma eligibility.
periods.recommendations: Keep the green result moving by sustaining fall senior conferences and requiring each high school to reconcile withdrawal codes, transfer documentation, and credit recovery enrollment before winter break. Add a targeted review of South Harbor and Airport Way seniors with two or more attendance-risk flags, and assign a named counselor or graduation coach to each student by cohort list.

periods.analysis: The graduation rate held steady at 91.3%, with a quarter-over-quarter movement of 0.0 from 2024-Q4. Holding green through the winter is meaningful because this is when attendance fatigue, family instability, and unfinished first-semester credits usually start to show up in the senior pipeline. The January diploma-readiness sweep found that most borderline students were clustered in English IV, Algebra recovery, and online civics modules run through the Harborview Learning Lab vendor portal. Stability is good news, but I read a flat quarter as an instruction to tighten execution rather than celebrate early.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the winter diploma-readiness sweep and require weekly completion reports from the Learning Lab for English IV, Algebra recovery, and civics modules. Extend Saturday credit labs at Bayside and Northport through March, with transportation aligned to Routes 14, 22, and the East Channel connector so attendance barriers do not become graduation barriers.

periods.analysis: The rate eased from 91.3% to 91.2%, a quarter-over-quarter change of -0.1, while still remaining green and above target. A one-tenth-point dip is small, but I pay attention to direction when we are approaching final transcript certification. Harborview’s growth continues to bring more late-arriving students, and the spring review showed a few unresolved records from out-of-state transfers and students temporarily housed through the family shelter network. The core system is healthy; the risk is not broad failure, it is losing a handful of students in the paperwork and attendance margins.
periods.recommendations: Sustain green performance by keeping the May transcript-certification room open daily until all senior records are cleared, with registrar support prioritized for late-arriving and shelter-connected students. Extend direct coordination between school registrars, the McKinney-Vento team, and Harborview Virtual Academy so no student misses graduation because a credit, assessment, or residency document is sitting in the wrong queue.

periods.analysis: The rate improved from 91.2% to 91.8%, a quarter-over-quarter gain of 0.6 points, strengthening our green position above the 90% target. This is the kind of movement I expect when adult follow-through meets student persistence. The Summer Bridge closeout, the Harborview Virtual Academy completion push, and campus-based counselor call nights appear to have pulled several near-completers across the finish line. The gain is real, and it also tells us which practices are worth institutionalizing before the next senior cohort enters its highest-risk months.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the Summer Bridge and Virtual Academy completion push as standing graduation infrastructure, not a one-time rescue effort. Extend counselor call nights into the first six weeks of the new school year for students with incomplete credits, verified employment conflicts, or chronic-absence histories, and publish a campus-by-campus near-completer list for principal review.

periods.analysis: The measure moved from 91.8% to 91.0%, a quarter-over-quarter change of -0.8, but it remains green and still above the 90% target. I take that decline seriously because the drop is larger than the prior quarter-to-quarter movements and it came during a period when chronic absenteeism pressure was visible in the ninth- and tenth-grade pipeline. Graduation remains strong, yet the early-warning data from Seaport High and West Bay showed more students off pace in core credits by the end of the first semester. This is not a red-light moment, but it is a clear instruction to protect the cohort before the senior year becomes a scramble.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the proven graduation practices while adding a fall-to-winter early-warning review for every 11th- and 12th-grade student with attendance below 90% or a failed core course. Extend credit-bearing attendance recovery blocks at Seaport High and West Bay, and require principals to report weekly on students who moved from off-track to back-on-track status.

periods.analysis: The rate rebounded from 91.0% to 91.9%, a quarter-over-quarter gain of 0.9 points, returning Harborview to the strongest result in this sequence. That improvement reflects disciplined cohort management: counselors, attendance specialists, and assistant principals did the unglamorous work of finding students, fixing schedules, and closing credit gaps. The midyear cohort audit showed particular improvement among students enrolled in dual-credit maritime logistics, airport operations, and health sciences pathways, where school felt connected to a real next step. Green at 91.9% is excellent, but the obligation now is to make the rebound durable rather than episodic.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the midyear cohort audit and formalize the pathway-student check-ins in maritime logistics, airport operations, and health sciences so career-connected students stay on track academically. Extend the same case-management protocol to non-pathway seniors, with every student below graduation pace assigned a named adult, a credit plan, and a weekly attendance target.

periods.analysis: The rate moved from 91.9% to 91.5%, a quarter-over-quarter change of -0.4, and remains green above the 90% target. After the strong rebound in 2026-Q1, this modest step down is manageable, but it tells me we still have sensitivity at the end of the year around attendance, make-up work, and final documentation. The spring certification team cleared most cases on schedule, though a small group of students needed late verification from Harborview Virtual Academy, adult education partners, and transfer schools outside the metro. Overall, Harborview is graduating students at a strong rate; the next level of work is reducing the number of students who require last-minute rescue.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the spring certification team and begin transcript verification earlier for students using virtual, adult education, or transfer credits. Extend a junior-year graduation-readiness conference to every campus by April, so credit gaps, attendance concerns, and assessment requirements are addressed before students enter their final senior cycle.

periods.analysis: Graduation is 91.2%, down from 91.5% in June but still above the 90% target. The small decline warrants attention to credit and transfer documentation without obscuring the on-target result.
periods.recommendations: Continue early transcript checks and flag rising seniors whose attendance or transfer credits need follow-up.
